World Watch: ten identity directions

A private OSINT dashboard that watches the whole world at once, follows connections and ownership chains, and shows only what sources report. Each direction below is a small identity system: concept, app icon with its small-size variant, wordmark, a colour system taken from a real agency or company palette (cited), two graphic devices that come from the concept, and four applications: the taskbar/Dock icon at real size, the top bar, a printed case-file cover for the Investigate page, and the splash screen.

Rules kept: original marks (no agency or company shape copied), real cited colours, no orange, readable at 16-24 px, no glowing globes or eyes.

TOP PICK 1 · 01

Cocked Hat

Three bearings never meet in a single point; the small triangle between them is where the truth lies, and its size says how sure you can be.

TOP PICK 2 · 06

W Trace

The initial of World Watch drawn as a signal burst on a quiet baseline: the world's signals and the name are the same line.

TOP PICK 3 · 02

Terminator

The shape night makes on the flat map of the world, computed for one real moment; the brand's main line is a fact, not a decoration.

Why these three. Cocked Hat turns the project's central rule (sources, and honesty about how sure we are) into geometry and has the stark one-accent temperament the owner likes. W Trace is the most legible mark at 16 px and the most 'defence tech'; its line can be real data in the app. Terminator is the calmest and the only one whose main line is a computed fact every time it is drawn. Runners-up: Shells (best fit for the Connections page) and Quadkey (the most personal: Munich's own tile address).

01

Cocked Hat Top pick 1

Three bearings never meet in a single point; the small triangle between them is where the truth lies, and its size says how sure you can be.

Navigators call it the cocked hat: take three bearings and they form a small triangle instead of a point. World Watch works the same way: it shows where independent sources agree and is honest about the spread. The mark is that triangle, the lines running off the edge because bearings are endless.

Honest notes

Why it works. The strongest idea in the set: it states the project's hard rule (sources, honesty about uncertainty) as geometry. Stark, monochrome plus one accent, closest to the Palantir/Anduril temperament without borrowing a shape.

Weaknesses. At 16 px it reads as an asterisk with a blue dot; the meaning needs the story once. The 'cocked hat' term is niche (navigation). Rotated 25 degrees so it does not read as the App Store's three-stroke 'A'.

02

Terminator Top pick 3

The shape night makes on the flat map of the world, computed for one real moment; the brand's main line is a fact, not a decoration.

On a flat world map the line between day and night is not straight: it bends into this flattened wave, and its shape changes with the season. The mark is the map window with night, twilight (sun 0 to 12 degrees below the horizon, as the app draws it) and day, computed for 28 Nov 2026 at 08:56 UTC.

03

Quadkey 1-2-0-2-3

The address of Munich on the web map: split the world in four, take one, repeat; the mark is the zoom from the whole world to the place where the watching starts.

Web maps cut the world into square tiles; each zoom level splits a tile in four, and a place's tile address is a string of digits called a quadkey. Munich's begins 1-2-0-2-3. Each lighter square is one zoom level, converging on the city. It also stands for the Connections page: open one layer, find the next inside it.

04

Great Circle

The straight line on the flat map is not the shortest way; the curve is. The mark keeps both, because World Watch shows things as they are, not as they look.

Every flight, cable and connection between two places on Earth follows a great circle, which bows towards the pole on a flat map. The dashed chord is the obvious line, the solid arc is the true one. Origin hollow, destination solid: a connection with a direction, the core of the Connections page.

05

Plot

On a radar scope the dots behind a target are where it really was; World Watch only ever draws positions someone actually reported.

Air traffic scopes leave a trail of history dots behind each target. They are not a line: the gaps are honest. The mark is a turning track: past reports in white, the newest one as the teal diamond pointing where it is heading. The project's rule 'never move anything ahead of its last report' made visible.

06

W Trace Top pick 2

The initial of World Watch drawn as a signal burst on a quiet baseline: the world's signals and the name are the same line.

Quakes, transponder pings and news spikes all arrive as a trace that is mostly flat with sudden bursts. Here the burst is the letter W. In the app the same trace is drawn from real counts (for example news per 15 minutes), so the brand's line is data whenever it appears.

07

GMT Bezel

A GMT watch tells the time in two places at once; World Watch tells you what is happening everywhere at once.

A watch made for pilots and navigators carries a 24-hour bezel, day on one half and night on the other, and one extra hand for another part of the world. Here the solid half is day, the faint half night, and the red pointer reaches into the night side: the half of the world that is asleep is still being watched.

08

Contact

Hull down: beyond the curve of the Earth the first thing you see of a ship is its mast, the moment a lookout exists for.

Because the Earth is round, a ship coming over the horizon shows its mast before its hull. A lookout's job is to catch that first sign. The mark is the curved sea, the sky and one mast: restrained, nautical, the alliance's two blues.

09

Shells

Open each shell until you reach the solid one: the person who really owns it.

Ownership chains hide behind holding companies inside holding companies. Registers such as the UK's 'people with significant control' exist to reach the end of the chain. The mark is two shells and a solid core pushed into the corner, the way the Connections page drills to a beneficial owner.

10

Footnote

W for World Watch with its reference mark: nothing on the screen appears without a source.

Every claim in a serious report carries a small number that leads to its source. The mark is the initial with that number in red. It is the editorial direction: the Investigate page as a well-sourced document, and the brand's promise that summaries are traceable.

How this was made, and what was dropped

  • Every mark is drawn on a 64-unit grid (plate corner radius 14, about the macOS/Fluent rounding); the same SVG is the 1024 master. A separate 16/24 px variant has heavier strokes and fewer parts, as Microsoft's Fluent guidance recommends below 48 px.
  • Renders are from headless Chromium at device scale 1. Windows draws a taskbar icon at 24 px at 100 % scale (16 px in title bars and context menus, 32 or 48 px at 200 %), so 16-24 px is the size that matters. On a Retina screen this page shows the 1x pixels enlarged; the real Dock would use 2x assets.
  • Wordmarks in the lockups are outlined (shaped with HarfBuzz, so kerning is applied); no font is needed to display them. All fonts are SIL OFL from Google Fonts and are embedded in this page as subsets.
  • Dropped after the small-size test: Racetrack (a surveillance orbit; read as a paperclip / link icon), Two hemispheres (read as cartoon eyes), Date line (the real line's jogs looked random), Morse WW (read as a bulleted list), Null Island (a crosshair). Earlier versions of Great Circle (read as a handbag), Plot (a paintbrush), GMT (a speedometer) and Cocked Hat (the App Store 'A') were redrawn.
  • Example values on device mock-ups are marked as such; the few real ones (RCH4992 capture, GLEIF relationship, Munich daylight, terminator) are labelled with their source or date.
  • Not verified here: UN Blue and ESA Deep Space could not be opened directly from this sandbox (403); both were confirmed through search excerpts of the official pages. NGA and Anduril colours come from their websites' own code, not from published brand guides; no public brand guide with colour values was found for NGA, NRO, Space Force (its Air Force instruction refused this sandbox), the Bundeswehr or the BND.
